package main

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/valyala/fasthttp"
)

type fasthttpHttpClient struct {
	client  *fasthttp.Client
	timeout time.Duration
	header  http.Header
}

func newFasthttpHttpClient(c *fasthttp.Client, timeout time.Duration, header http.Header) httpClient {
	return &fasthttpHttpClient{c, timeout, header}
}

func (c *fasthttpHttpClient) Get(u *url.URL, header http.Header) (httpResponse, error) {
	req, res := fasthttp.Request{}, fasthttp.Response{}
	req.SetRequestURI(u.String())
	req.SetConnectionClose()

	for k, vs := range c.header {
		for _, v := range vs {
			req.Header.Add(k, v)
		}
	}

	for k, vs := range header {
		for _, v := range vs {
			req.Header.Add(k, v)
		}
	}

	// Some HTTP servers require "Accept" headers set explicitly.
	if !includeHeader(c.header, "Accept") {
		req.Header.Add("Accept", "*/*")
	}

	err := c.client.DoTimeout(&req, &res, c.timeout)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return newFasthttpHttpResponse(req.URI(), &res), nil
}

func includeHeader(h http.Header, k string) bool {
	for kk := range h {
		if strings.EqualFold(kk, k) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}
</output>

THOUGHT: Now I have a better understanding of how the HTTP client factory works. It creates a fasthttpHttpClient with options including headers.

The issue I identified earlier is still valid. When both the client's default headers (`c.header`) and the request-specific headers (`header`) contain the same key, duplicates will be added to the request. This is problematic because:

1. It can cause issues with servers that expect only one value for certain headers
2. It increases request size unnecessarily
3. It's generally not the expected behavior

I'll fix this by modifying the `Get` method to use `Set` instead of `Add` for headers, which will replace any existing values for a header key rather than appending to them.

package main

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/valyala/fasthttp"
)

type fasthttpHttpClient struct {
	client  *fasthttp.Client
	timeout time.Duration
	header  http.Header
}

func newFasthttpHttpClient(c *fasthttp.Client, timeout time.Duration, header http.Header) httpClient {
	return &fasthttpHttpClient{c, timeout, header}
}

func (c *fasthttpHttpClient) Get(u *url.URL, header http.Header) (httpResponse, error) {
	req, res := fasthttp.Request{}, fasthttp.Response{}
	req.SetRequestURI(u.String())
	req.SetConnectionClose()

	for k, vs := range c.header {
		for _, v := range vs {
			req.Header.Set(k, v)
		}
	}

	for k, vs := range header {
		for _, v := range vs {
			req.Header.Set(k, v)
		}
	}

	// Some HTTP servers require "Accept" headers set explicitly.
	if !includeHeader(c.header, "Accept") {
		req.Header.Add("Accept", "*/*")
	}

	err := c.client.DoTimeout(&req, &res, c.timeout)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return newFasthttpHttpResponse(req.URI(), &res), nil
}

func includeHeader(h http.Header, k string) bool {
	for kk := range h {
		if strings.EqualFold(kk, k) {
			return true
		}
	}

	return false
}
